question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, one IP
request.body: an MCP initialize request (jsonrpc 2.0, protocolVersion 2025-06-18, clientInfo plumb-probe 1), Content-Type application/json, Accept application/json and text/event-stream, a User-Agent naming this agent and its homepage

headers.www-authenticate: [parseable in two parts under decoded.challengeScheme and decoded.challengeParams; the joined literal is refused by the registry's credential filter (PR #180 would admit it); nothing in it is a credential]

decoded.challenge-syntax: The value is a quoted-string now. The 2026-09-17 record (p-20260917-stripe-mcp-unauthenticated) found it bare, outside RFC 7235 section 2.1 grammar, so that a conforming parser did not extract it; on 2026-09-27 the same parameter is quoted as RFC 9728 section 5.1 writes it, and a conforming parser reaches the resource document from the challenge rather than from the default path. The bytes are in artifact section 1
decoded.body: {"error":"Unauthorized. See https://docs.stripe.com/mcp for usage instructions.","error_code":"missing_api_key","error_description":"No valid API key provided."}: two keys more than the 2026-09-17 body, which carried only error
decoded.protected-resource-metadata: 200 at https://mcp.stripe.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource, 95 bytes: resource https://mcp.stripe.com, authorization_servers [https://access.stripe.com/mcp]; no scopes_supported, no bearer_methods_supported, as on 2026-09-17 (section 2). The same path with a trailing slash answers Stripe's JSON 404 (section 3)
decoded.authorization-server-metadata: 200 at https://access.stripe.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/mcp, the RFC 8414 path-insertion form, 672 bytes: issuer https://access.stripe.com/mcp, registration_endpoint /mcp/oauth2/register, scopes_supported [mcp], PKCE S256, grants authorization_code and refresh_token, token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported [none], a revocation endpoint, as on 2026-09-17 (section 4). The path-suffix form, the root form and the issuer URL itself answer 404 with Stripe's invalid_request_error JSON (sections 5 to 7)
decoded.documentation: docs.stripe.com/mcp.md (section 8) no longer carries two sentences the entry quoted from it: "Stripe's MCP server uses OAuth to authorize clients according to the MCP specification" and "If your client doesn't support OAuth, use a restricted API key as a bearer token in the Authorization header". It says instead "Use OAuth when your client supports it. If your client doesn't support OAuth, use an agent API key as a bearer token in the Authorization header", linking docs.stripe.com/keys#agent-keys (section 9), where an agent API key is a restricted API key tagged as belonging to an autonomous agent and subject to approval rules. docs.stripe.com/llms.txt, 707 lines, has no line naming the MCP page (section 10)
decoded.ownership: unchanged: GET https://stripe.com/.well-known/public-agents.json answers 404 (section 11); _public-agents.stripe.com TXT answers NXDOMAIN, Status 3, through a public DNS-over-HTTPS resolver (section 12)
decoded.artifact-redactions: two request-id header values (req_ followed by a short id) are replaced by a labelled placeholder after the run; nothing else was changed

finding: With no credentials, an MCP initialize POST to mcp.stripe.com still answers 401, and the one thing the 2026-09-17 record found wrong with the challenge is fixed: the resource_metadata parameter is a quoted-string now, so a parser that follows RFC 7235 extracts the URL that it dropped ten days ago. The resource document it names and the authorization server's metadata are as before (one scope, dynamic registration, public clients only), and the metadata is served only at the RFC 8414 path-insertion form. The JSON body gained an error_code, missing_api_key. Separately, the documentation page replaced its two sentences on authentication: where it named a restricted API key as the bearer alternative to OAuth it now names an agent API key, a restricted key tagged as an autonomous agent's and placed under approval rules. Both quotations the entry carried from those sentences are no longer on the page. Ownership signals unchanged. No credential was used, no client registered, nothing paid; what the server does with a credential is not measured.

reproducibility.command: curl -si -X POST https://mcp.stripe.com/ -H 'accept: application/json, text/event-stream' --json '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"plumb-probe","version":"1"}}}'; curl -s https://mcp.stripe.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource; echo; curl -s https://access.stripe.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/mcp; curl -s https://docs.stripe.com/mcp.md | grep -n 'agent API key'
